text:
miguel: RFC follow-up: new 'preempt window' idea for Frontdoor -> edge gateways to reclaim long-lived streams under pressure. thoughts on lifecycle and hedging?

anna: sketch the flow pls.

miguel: Frontdoor marks connection preemptable at OPEN, issues signed token T (id|expiry|epoch). It injects header `x-rw-preempt: T` to upstream. On reclaim, Frontdoor sends REVOKE {id, epoch}. Gateway treats REVOKE as soft first (send end-of-stream hint), then hard cut after drain_timeout.

sam: flow example:
Client -> Frontdoor: OPEN {id, tenant, preemptable=true}
Frontdoor -> Upstream: request + headers { x-rw-preempt: T }
...streaming...
Frontdoor -> Upstream: REVOKE {id, epoch} // soft revoke
Upstream: finish inflight tokens or close after drain_timeout

irene: concerns: 1) mid-stream side effects if cut, 2) hedging/late-bind where multiple upstream copies exist.

sam: hedging approach: include epoch+nonce in T so only matching upstream honors REVOKE; hedged copies ignore unless token epoch matches. This requires token to be consistently propagated to fanouts.

anna: security: tokens must be HMAC-signed and short-lived. format: `T = base64(id|expiry|epoch|hmac)`.

irene: observability: emit span events `revoke=soft|hard`, counters `revoke.soft`/`revoke.hard`, and log tenant/quota-bucket.

miguel: ops: avoid thrash on mass revokes 5 randomize drain_timeout or use per-tenant backoff. CPU cost for HMAC verify per stream is small but measurable.

ops-bot: simulated revoke sweep at 16:02 UTC: avg drain latency 200ms; 0 upstream 5xx. :white_check_mark:

sam: impl note: prefer opaque signed tokens so gateways can verify locally; maintain tiny recent-epoch bitmap for hard-revokes.

anna: I'll prototype token shape + verification snippet by EOW.

miguel: I'll open RFC PR with diagrams, perf estimates, and proposed headers. @sam add hedging interaction. Canary: tenant-scoped revokes only.

ops-bot: reminder: create RFC issue link when ready.
